input.question: If Oil prices have dropped close to 40% per barrel, why has diesel only dropped 10% at the pump [UK]
input.ground_truth: Because the price at the pump isn't solely determined by price per barrel. Refining it still costs the same and the government and/or state taxes don't change. I also costs the same amount to transport. Also, 1 barrel of oil (42 gallons) translates into about 10 gallons of diesel when refined.

Okay, let’s imagine oil is like a big chocolate bar, and the price of the chocolate bar goes down a lot. But the chocolate bar is made up of smaller pieces inside — some are for making candy (that’s like gasoline), and some are for making chocolate milk (that’s a bit like diesel).

When the whole chocolate bar gets cheaper, you might think every little piece inside also gets much cheaper. But here’s the thing: the way we turn the big chocolate bar into candy or chocolate milk isn’t the same for both. Making chocolate milk (diesel) takes a special recipe and some extra steps, and sometimes those steps cost a lot of money too.

Also, the people who sell chocolate milk at the shop (the petrol stations) don’t always lower their prices as much as the chocolate bar got cheaper. They might keep the price a bit higher because they have other costs, like paying for the shop and the people who work there.

So, when the big chocolate bar (oil) gets a lot cheaper, the chocolate milk (diesel) at the shop only gets a little bit cheaper. That’s why diesel didn’t drop as much as oil did!
